entities.summary:
Ferenc Frangepán was a Hungarian nobleman and Latinist who played a crucial role in the preservation of classical knowledge during the tumultuous 16th century. 
Born in Modruš, Croatia in 1490, Frangepán's family had long been associated with the Hungarian nobility, but it was his own intellectual pursuits that would set him apart from his contemporaries.

As a prominent Latinist and scholar of classical languages, Frangepán was instrumental in translating and preserving ancient texts, including works by Cicero and Virgil. His efforts helped to ensure the continuation of classical learning during a period marked by significant cultural upheaval.

Frankopan's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his work laid the groundwork for future generations of scholars and intellectuals. Today, Frangepán is recognized as one of the most important figures in Hungarian intellectual history, and his contributions to the preservation of classical knowledge continue to be celebrated.

The passing of Ferenc Frangepán on February 7, 1543, marked the end of an era, but his impact on the world of learning would endure for centuries to come.
